problem: Web screens are often composed from visible content or a preferred style before the end-to-end journey, role and situation differences, reachable states, evidence needs, and action priorities are established. The current product-design Guides can rank and render an already-framed screen but do not require this information-architecture and user-flow model or a bounded handoff to interactive-web-motion.
reusable_when: Structuring a web page or multi-page flow around user tasks, decisions, and evidence
Choosing element placement and emphasis for different roles, situations, permissions, and reachable states
Designing dashboards, onboarding, forms, decision-support pages, and service journeys with clear entry, exit, recovery, and continuation
Deciding whether a need is satisfied by static structure or requires a separate interaction or scroll-motion decision
not_for: Pure typography, color, or visual-style changes with no information-architecture or task-flow decision
Detailed motion choreography, scroll-trigger mechanics, animation accessibility, or runtime performance owned by interactive-web-motion
Marketing positioning, claims, and copy strategy owned by marketing
Backend orchestration, authorization enforcement, or business-policy decisions
existing_coverage: product-design owns design briefs, typography, visual hierarchy, generic interaction states, responsive accessibility, and reference selection. interactive-web-motion separately owns motion intent, choreography, scroll-triggered and scroll-linked behavior, motion accessibility, and runtime verification. This candidate adds one information-architecture and user-flow Guide to product-design and preserves the motion Pack boundary.

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Pages mirror an organization, component library, or default persona instead of the user's end-to-end task, causing misplaced emphasis, duplicate or hidden actions, role-state dead ends, inconsistent continuity, and unjustified interaction.
decision_checks: Define the user's problem, desired outcome, entry context, constraints, and end-to-end journey before fixing page boundaries
Map roles and situations by task, frequency, experience, permissions, evidence needs, and reachable states rather than demographics alone
Give every page, section, and prominent element a traceable user question, decision, proof need, or next action
Choose primary, secondary, destructive, recovery, and deferred actions per role and state instead of making all actions equally prominent
Preserve meaning across visual order, programmatic reading order, focus order, responsive reflow, navigation labels, and repeated controls
Expose entry, continuation, completion, cancellation, correction, empty, loading, failure, retry, undo, and permission-denied paths that the product can reach
Use interaction only for feedback, state change, continuity, orientation, disclosure, or decision support; hand detailed motion and scroll behavior to interactive-web-motion
Verify the structure with representative content and task evidence across role, state, input, and viewport variations

pass_criteria: Information-architecture and role-state flow requests select the local Guide together with no more than three inherited product-design Guides
Every prominent element and action can be traced to a user need, journey step, role or situation, reachable state, or evidence requirement
The Guide requires meaningful visual, reading, focus, responsive, and cross-page continuity
Explicit motion and scroll-specific requests remain owned by interactive-web-motion
regression_criteria: Backend, marketing-only, and motion-specific requests are not hijacked
The Guide does not prescribe universal coordinates, one-thing-per-page, progressive disclosure, or a single persona as default truth
The Pack never grants repository or external write authority
Unrendered structure and unsupported user assumptions are never reported as verified
